summary: Phase 3.7.3 P0 regression — Orion 'Widget Not Found' + LLM 403 fixes verified end-to-end on the preview env (https://realm-deploy.preview.emergentagent.com). 9/9 pytest cases pass (Health endpoint 200/403/401 RBAC, chat replies for Hello/What is your name?/Help, founder-briefing analytics intercept, unknown-widget 404, registry-delete self-heal). Frontend smoke: `[Orion] backend health check ok (6 checks)` logged twice on mount, all 13 non-soon sidebar nav items render cleanly, Cmd+K palette opens / filters 'brief' → row 0 = 'Founder Briefing (Section)' / closes on Esc, all 6 quick action tiles dispatch to Orion Chat (chat-active=true). Zero Orion-related console errors.
critical_code_review_comments: orion_health.py:DASHBOARD_TILES uses hyphen ids ('founder-briefing','investor-snapshot','draft-badge','draft-widget','create-announcement','support-digest') but AdminOrion.jsx QUICK_TILES uses underscore ids ('founder_briefing','investor','draft_badge','draft_widget','announcement','support_digest'). The check still passes (no cross-validation done), but the 'dashboard_tiles' health check is informational-only; if E1 later upgrades the check to verify FE/BE parity it will mismatch. Recommend either renaming QUICK_TILE ids or updating DASHBOARD_TILES to match QUICK_TILES.id.

widget_chat.py:_heal_orion_registry uses upsert + $setOnInsert with auto_healed=true — correctly idempotent. Verified via the self-heal test: deleted row, called chat, row reappeared with auto_healed=true, second call kept exactly 1 row (no duplicates).

chat_conversations.py:call_openai_chat fallback chain is sound. With current OPENAI_API_KEY working in preview, attempt 1 succeeds — emergent fallback path is exercised only via unit-level injection. Confirmed clean 503 contract on dry-run by reading the code path; no Cloudflare 502 observed across 20+ chat calls during testing.

AdminOrion.jsx:198 startup validation useEffect logs at info-level — good, won't pollute Sentry. Twin log emission (`backend health check ok` printed twice) is React StrictMode double-invoke in dev — harmless in prod build.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (sidebar 13/13, tiles 6/6, palette 3/3 scenarios, health log present)
